authority_basis.scope: Verified arXiv:2606.28052v1 and its scoped implications for Marici modular completion

operations.title: Zhu–He–Han — Planar loop integrands from cuts in (D) dimensions
operations.summary: Primary source proving universal Möbius reconstruction of planar colored loop integrands from canonical non-scaleless cut data.

operations.title: Planar colored loop reconstruction is Möbius inversion on the admissible cut-refinement poset
operations.summary: For the finite poset P of admissible non-scaleless planar topologies, canonical cuts are the zeta transform of irreducible numerator data; the inverse Möbius element reconstructs the integrand, with theory-independent coefficients and theory dependence confined to cut functions.

operations.title: Intertwining minimal spanning cuts and generating refinements suffices to intertwine planar Möbius reconstruction
operations.summary: If a theory-producing operation E, especially J1, preserves the admissible/scaleless quotient, tree gluing and internal-state descent, and commutes with every generating residue from minimal spanning cuts, then E commutes with the complete planar reconstructed integrand.

operations.title: The cut-refinement incidence algebra is the Euler shadow of a derived incidence category of scalar degenerations
operations.summary: The coefficients gamma=1-chi(CW) should arise from shifted reduced cellular complexes and their refinement correspondences; modular completion is then derived incidence assembly, with ordinary Möbius inversion its decategorification.

operations.title: Möbius reconstruction does not make raw Cut data conservative before the admissible quotient
operations.summary: The theorem is planar and organized after excluding scaleless sectors; it does not recover Cut-invisible contact/UV classes or prove nonplanar, uncolored, scalar-scaffolded, or chain-level compatibility.

operations.title: Minimal-cut and refinement-edge naturality test for J1
operations.summary: On one fixed planar (n,L) poset, verify J1 on every minimal spanning cut and every single-propagator refinement edge, including scaleless-ideal preservation and internal-state gluing, then compare the two Möbius-reconstructed integrands.

operations.title: Categorified Möbius versus scalar Cousin-totalization test
operations.summary: Replace gamma(Gamma)=1-chi(CW(Gamma)) by the shifted reduced cellular complex of CW(Gamma), test functorial composition under refinement, and compare its Euler shadow and orientation/torsion data with the scalar surface Cousin complex.

operations.reason: The primary paper derives the cut relation as a zeta transform on a finite refinement poset and reconstructs the canonical planar integrand by the inverse Möbius function.

evidence.paraphrase: Equations 13–17 derive the universal Möbius coefficients; the abstract and section 3 separate universal reconstruction from theory-dependent D-dimensional tree gluing.

operations.reason: Möbius naturality would propagate a correctly typed transformation of cut diagrams, but no scalar-scaffolding theorem yet proves J1 compatibility with generating refinements, the scaleless quotient, and internal-state descent.

evidence.paraphrase: The paper states that minimal spanning cuts generate higher cuts by further residues, but does not study J1 or scalar-derived normal operations.

operations.reason: The equality gamma=1-chi(CW) gives a canonical Euler-characteristic shadow, while Marici's orientation, torsion and secondary classes require a chain-level refinement rather than scalar coefficients alone.

evidence.paraphrase: The reconstruction coefficient is one minus the Euler characteristic of a topology-dependent CW complex assembled from refinement intervals.
